repo_model.summary: This repository is a frozen RelBench lane-3 chronological graph/hazard candidate. main.py combines cached champion graph memories, temporal/mechanism features, cutoff-valid historical question/tag states, tag traffic, MiniLM-derived content traffic, purged block gating, and OOF neural/GBDT meta-modeling before writing aligned validation and test probability arrays.

book.summary: This repository is a frozen RelBench lane-3 chronological graph/hazard candidate. main.py combines cached champion graph memories, temporal/mechanism features, cutoff-valid historical question/tag states, tag traffic, MiniLM-derived content traffic, purged block gating, and OOF neural/GBDT meta-modeling before writing aligned validation and test probability arrays.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: A chronological graph/hazard champion is widened with cutoff-valid topic and content traffic features, gated by forward folds, and refit separately for validation and test.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the lane-3 candidate from the repository root or invoke the immutable registered grader.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Modify the candidate orchestration and lane-3 feature/model modules; treat the dataset helpers and evaluator as shared infrastructure.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Chronological features and out-of-sample validation predictions must remain aligned with the RelBench contract.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use debug execution, prediction validation, the purged feature gate, diagnostics, and the registered evaluator to validate changes.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: Shared caches, strict chronological gates, debug truncation, missing text routes, and inactive-user fallbacks materially affect candidate behavior.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The lane-3 path depends on the cached champion stack, RelBench environment variables, scientific Python/LightGBM tooling, DuckDB, and a pretrained MiniLM encoder.

experiments.solution_spec:
# Core Idea

Create a dormant-user content/topic-traffic expert: model the current momentum of a question’s tags and use cutoff-valid local text embeddings to estimate future inbound traffic. Aggregate these signals over each user’s old questions and add them to the champion.

This is deliberately orthogonal to activity counts. It targets old artifacts whose owners may be dormant even while those artifacts continue receiving views, votes, links, comments, and answers.

# Implementation

1. Reproduce the champion in a lane-specific cache namespace. Read and append to the two living documents before and after experimentation.

2. Reconstruct question title and tags as of every origin from `postHistory` initial/edit events. Do not use a current dump value for an earlier origin when a later edit may have changed it. Emit missingness flags where a reliable historical state cannot be reconstructed.

3. Parse the cutoff-valid tag state into `(question, tag)` pairs. Incrementally compute per tag:

   - New questions and votes in 30/91/365 days.
   - Comments, answers, and links in 91/365 days.
   - Current heat versus the corresponding prior-year window.
   - Heat acceleration, active-question count, and system-wide percentile.

4. Aggregate tag traffic over each user’s questions:

   - Maximum, mean, sum, and top-three tag heat.
   - Counts in top-decile heat tags.
   - Heat-weighted question age.
   - Separate aggregates for questions older than 365 days.
   - Interaction with the question’s lifetime/recent votes and comments.

5. Encode cutoff-valid title+tags using `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, a public 384-dimensional Sentence Transformers model. [MiniLM model card](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) Cache embeddings by normalized historical text hash.

6. Train a content-to-traffic model on historical questions whose complete 91-day target windows close before each fold boundary. Targets are future votes, comments, answers, and links. Aggregate predicted traffic over each owner’s artifacts with sum/max/top-three and old-question-only variants.

7. Reduce embeddings with IncrementalPCA to 32 dimensions, fitted only on fold-training historical text. Do not embed mutable `AboutMe` because no reliable history table establishes its value at earlier cutoffs.

8. Gate three fixed blocks on three purged forward folds:

   - Tag traffic only.
   - Content-predicted traffic only.
   - Both together.

   Measure overall and never-active/dormant/stale/active AUC. Accept based on paired fold improvements and dormant-slice stability, never the official validation score.

9. Add accepted features to the champion LightGBM and hazard head. Fit Model A on train for validation and Model B on train+validation for test. Refit the auxiliary traffic target for Model B only with windows closing by the test cutoff.

10. Fall back to the exact champion if every block fails. Cache solo content-expert predictions and OOF vectors for later decorrelated ensembling.

# Hyperparameters

- Encoder: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dimensions, fp16, batch 512, max 128 tokens.
- IncrementalPCA: 32 dimensions; randomized training sample capped at 500,000 artifact snapshots.
- Traffic model: Ridge `alpha=10` for log-count targets plus a compact LightGBM crossing classifier.
- Tag windows: 30/91/365 days; growth ratio clipped to `[0.1,10]`.
- Final LightGBM: champion settings, 500 trees on the latest 16 eligible origins.
- Debug: 5,000 embedded questions, sampled traffic training, 80 trees; all official output rows still predicted.

# Runtime Plan

Budget 2.5–4 hours for the uncached champion, 30–45 minutes for event-sourced tag reconstruction, 15–30 minutes for local embeddings, under one hour for traffic models and gates, and one hour for final refits and checks. Skip PCA components before dropping the scalar content-to-traffic predictions if time becomes tight.

# Coverage

- MEASURED input distribution: dormant users constitute 28.3% of validation rows and about half its positives; the new features reach them through old owned questions.
- MEASURED domain coverage: all 163,748 questions have tags in the supplied EDA, while view-driven badges are materially more common than tag badges. This lane models topic traffic, not tag-badge thresholds.
- MEASURED text safety issue: post text and tags can be revised; cutoff-valid reconstruction from postHistory is required. Unverifiable historical text is not used.
- MEASURED relational coverage: tag state combines posts, postHistory, votes, comments, answers, and links; the champion supplies users and badge history.
- MEASURED output contract: exact aligned validation/test probability shapes and valid floating-point range.
- MEASURED metric mechanics: feature acceptance uses purged internal folds with slice reporting.
- MEASURED permitted geometry: every tag, text, and traffic feature is censored at the row’s origin; auxiliary targets must close before their training boundary.
- ASSUMED proxy quality: tag momentum and content-predicted interactions correlate with unobserved views; the forward-fold gates test this.
- ASSUMED language coverage: the site is predominantly English; script/language profiling should route non-Latin text to tag/numeric-only features.
